prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: WALL WEATHERING DECAL TEXTURE ATLAS for a realistic abandoned zombie horror environment. These marks must look attached to vertical painted plaster/concrete walls.
Maximum detail, 4K landscape 3840 x 2160 if supported. Actual transparent RGBA background, with soft semitransparent edges and transparent gaps. EXACTLY EIGHT completely separate irregular decals in a strict 4-column by 2-row atlas, in reading order. Center each mark in its own cell, keep its entire silhouette and any flecks within central 65% of the cell. Wide completely transparent gutters between all marks, no overlap, no clipping, no touching the canvas borders. Each mark must be fully isolated and usable individually on an existing wall texture.
Photorealistic photographed material microtexture; orthographic straight-on view; neutral diffuse light, no dramatic shadows, no cast shadow behind mark. Only the localized damage/stain should be visible; do NOT include a wall panel, rectangular background, slab, floating rock, frame or substrate surrounding the effect. No full scene, no floor dirt piles, no mud puddles, no footprints, no tire tracks, no hands, no actual claw or tool, no blood, no people, no text or watermark, no visible grid or borders. Natural uneven scale, restrained abandoned-building palette.
Eight WALL SURFACE SCRATCH AND SCUFF DECALS: 1 cluster of three long thin diagonal scratches through aged light-gray paint, exposing darker plaster in the narrow gouges; 2 rough horizontal scrape with paint rubbed away irregularly; 3 five parallel ragged claw-like scratches gouged into plaster, believable shallow wall damage only; 4 patch of many fine hairline scratch marks crossing in varied directions, subtle worn surface; 5 broad dark-gray abrasion/scuff with soft fading edges from repeated contact; 6 short vertical chipped scratch cluster with a few tiny paint flakes remaining at its edges; 7 long single branching jagged scratch with small chipped borders; 8 irregular rubbed patch of worn paint with rough exposed plaster microtexture. Show the scratches themselves with only narrow local damaged borders, not broad opaque painted patches.
